name: Basilica of Regina Pacis
history: During World War II, the pastor of St. Rosalia's urged his Bensonhurst parish to build a votive shrine to Mary, Queen of Peace, for the safe return of its men and for a just peace. Ground was broken on 3 October 1948 and the shrine was dedicated on 15 August 1951. Benedict XVI named it a basilica in 2012.
arch: Italian Renaissance Revival, built entirely of marble from different parts of Italy, with two pulpits in the manner of Italian cathedrals. It was one of the first air-conditioned churches in America.
features: The 52-foot ceiling mural shows the Coronation of Mary, with Pope Pius XII blessing the shrine below.
Parishioners donated their own jewellery to make gold crowns for the image of Mary and the Child.

look.d: An Italian bell tower in Brooklyn's Little Italy of Bensonhurst.
The crowns were stolen days after the coronation, and mailed back a week later; parishioners call it a miracle.

fun: The crowns were stolen again in 1973 and recovered 12 days later from an airline terminal locker.
journal: A peace shrine paid for in wedding rings and earrings. Italian marble, Brooklyn heart.

a: As a votive for safe return from WWII and for peace
